newsitem.title: USA: Sonus product to resume FDA review process.
newsitem.headline: Sonus product to resume FDA review process.

text.p: Sonus Pharmaceuticals Inc said Tuesday it was prepared to resume a formal review of its EchoGen ultrasound contrast agents following a U.S. Food and Drug Administration determination that these agents will be regulated as drugs.

The company last September filed a New Drug Application seeking approval of its contrast agents for cardiology and radiology indications, but that process was delayed when competing companies developing similar products sought to have them classified as medical devices rather than drugs.

After learning of the FDA determination, Sonus President and Chief Executive Officer Dr. Steven Quay told Reuters he saw a "good chance" Sonus would be the first company to win approval of an ultrasound contrast diagnostic agent. Companies working on similar drugs include the Italian company Bracco, Molecular Biosystems Inc and DuPont Merck, a joint venture of DuPont Co and Merck and Co Inc.
"(The ruling) is positive for Sonus," Quay said. "It gets our FDA review back on track and makes a level playing field for all the companies developing these agents."
Ultrasound contrast agents are substances containing fluorinated gases that when injected into the bloodstream reflect soundwaves, helping to create clearer pictures.
